sources.zFor.monotone: scipy.stats.norm.isf(alpha / 2); the property compares neighbours of the list
sources.quantile.order-statistics: the i-th order statistic at p = i / (n - 1), by sorting
sources.quantile.interpolation: type 7 in exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction) at rational p
sources.quantile.small-samples: n = 1 returns the value, n = 2 interpolates linearly (exact rationals)
sources.quantile.ties: numpy.quantile(method='linear') on samples with repeated values
sources.quantile.unsorted: numpy.quantile(method='linear') on samples in random order
sources.unreliability.constant: a constant sample has no spread: 0
sources.unreliability.pass-flags: numpy.quantile on 0/1 flags: the share of fails between the deciles
sources.sampleVariance.offset: exact rational arithmetic on values with a large common offset
sources.sampleVariance.tiny-spread: exact rational arithmetic on values that differ in the 12th digit
sources.sampleVariance.mixed-scale: exact rational arithmetic on values of both signs and mixed magnitude
sources.sampleVariance.constant: a constant sample has variance exactly 0
sources.designEffect.no-clustering: m = 1 or rho = 0 gives 1, in exact rationals
sources.designEffect.negative-rho: 1 + (m - 1) rho with -1 / (m - 1) < rho < 0, in exact rationals
sources.designEffect.fractional-m: 1 + (m - 1) rho with a non-integer m, in exact rationals
sources.effectiveSampleSize.no-clustering: n unchanged when m = 1 or rho = 0
sources.effectiveSampleSize.negative-rho: n / (1 + (m - 1) rho), above n for a negative rho, in exact rationals
sources.effectiveSampleSize.fractional: n / (1 + (m - 1) rho) with a non-integer n or m, in exact rationals
sources.goodTuring.zero-counts: classes with count 0 are not observed
sources.goodTuring.fields: n, observed, f1 and f2 by direct counting
sources.hillNumber.uniform: k equally common classes have Hill number k at every order
sources.hillNumber.single-class: one class has Hill number 1 at every order
sources.hillNumber.richness-ignores-zeros: order 0 counts the classes with a positive count
sources.hillNumber.simpson: order 2 is 1 / sum p^2, in exact rational arithmetic
sources.hillNumber.shannon: order 1 is exp(-sum p ln p), by math.log and math.exp
sources.hillNumber.scale-free: the Hill number depends on proportions only: counts times a constant give the same value
sources.hillNumbers.orders: the three orders 0, 1 and 2 by direct computation
sources.hillNumbers.ordered: q0 >= q1 >= q2 >= 1 for every sample (Hill numbers fall as the order rises)
sources.icc.one-level: variance at the single named level over the total
sources.icc.two-levels: cumulative variance over the total, two named levels
sources.icc.three-levels: cumulative variance over the total, three named levels
sources.icc.zero-total: no variance anywhere: every correlation 0, no division by zero
sources.icc.last-level-reaches-share: the correlation of the last named level is one minus the residual share
sources.neymanAllocation.integer-optimum: brute force over every integer allocation of the total (exact rational objective)
sources.neymanAllocation.sums-to-total: the allocation is a whole number per stratum and sums to the total
sources.neymanAllocation.zero-spread: when every spread is 0 the allocation is proportional to the sizes
sources.neymanAllocation.every-stratum-sampled: a stratum with spread gets at least one unit when the total allows it, since its variance is infinite otherwise
sources.pageHinkley.before-minimum: no alarm can fire before minInstances points; the statistics still accumulate
sources.pageHinkley.alarm-up: an increase of the mean raises the up statistic past the threshold
sources.pageHinkley.alarm-down: a decrease of the mean raises the down statistic past the threshold
sources.pageHinkley.reset-after-alarm: all state resets after an alarm, so a second change fires a second alarm
sources.pageHinkley.delta-tolerance: a larger delta tolerates a larger drift before the statistic grows
sources.pageHinkley.min-instances-boundary: the statistic crosses the threshold early, but no alarm fires before minInstances points: the alarm sits on point minInstances exactly
sources.pageHinkley.quiet-series: a series without change stays under the threshold: no alarm
sources.pairedRateDifference.positive-covariance: bothPass * bothFail > regressed * improved: phi corrected by n / 2, floored at 0
sources.pairedRateDifference.negative-covariance: bothPass * bothFail < regressed * improved: phi not corrected
sources.pairedRateDifference.zero-margin: a zero margin makes phi 0 (the denominator would vanish)
sources.pairedRateDifference.extreme-tables: every pair regressed or every pair improved: the interval sits against the end of [-1, 1] (the Wilson limits there are exact)
sources.pairedRateDifference.sign: the estimate is the baseline rate minus the candidate rate: positive when the candidate regressed
sources.pairedRateDifference.swap-mirrors: swapping regressed and improved negates the estimate and mirrors the interval
sources.nonInferiority.clear-parity: identical results over many pairs: non-inferior at a 10 point margin
sources.nonInferiority.clear-regression: a large drop is not within the margin
sources.nonInferiority.margin-boundary: the verdict flips when the margin crosses the upper bound of the effect interval (strict inequality)
sources.nonInferiority.gating-flag: a gating flag firing for the candidate and not the baseline blocks parity even when the rates agree
sources.nonInferiority.named-pairs: the regressed and the newly flagged pairs are listed by name
sources.repeatsForFloor.difference: a floor on a difference of two versions doubles the variance
sources.repeatsForFloor.single-version: a floor on one version does not double it
sources.repeatsForFloor.blocks: averaging more blocks lowers the repeats in proportion
sources.repeatsForFloor.custom-z: the z of the floor is a parameter
sources.repeatsForFloor.flip-rate: a flip rate p gives the variance p (1 - p)
sources.repeatsForFloor.integer-ratio: when the ratio is exactly an integer it is not rounded up
sources.repeatsForFloor.floor-reached: the floor reported is the half-width that many repeats give
sources.binomialCdf.exact-small: exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction) with dyadic p, so the float p is the exact p
sources.binomialCdf.edges: k below 0 is 0, k at or above n is 1, p = 0 and p = 1 are point masses
sources.binomialCdf.upper-tail: exact rational arithmetic near k = n, where the cdf is close to 1
sources.binomialCdf.lower-tail-tiny: exact rational arithmetic for probabilities down to about 1e-57: relative accuracy in the far tail
sources.zeroFailureBound.table: ceil(ln alpha / ln(1 - p)) in 80-digit decimal arithmetic on the exact doubles
sources.zeroFailureBound.exact-integers: p and alpha such that (1 - p)^n = alpha exactly for a whole n, as written in decimal (0.9 and 0.001 give 3) or in binary: the answer is n, not n + 1
sources.zeroFailureBound.tiny-p: p below 1e-6: ln(1 - p) must be computed without losing digits (80-digit decimals)
sources.zeroFailureBound.large-p: p close to 1: one or two units
sources.reduceRepeats.mode: mode: the most common scored value when more than half of the repeats are scored; a tie goes to the value seen first (the documented rule, restated)
sources.reduceRepeats.median: median: above one half passes, below fails, exactly one half is undecided
sources.reduceRepeats.at-least: at_least k: passes at k passes, fails when the passes plus the unscored cannot reach k, else undecided
sources.reduceRepeats.unscored-left-out: an unscored repeat is left out of every reducer: the same verdicts with and without it where the rule allows
sources.abundances.number-and-string-differ: the number 1 and the string '1' are two labels
sources.abundances.counts-sum: the counts sum to the number of labels and there is one per distinct label
sources.mulberry32.seed-wrap: the seed is taken modulo 2^32 (JavaScript ToUint32): negative seeds and seeds above 2^32 wrap
sources.mulberry32.long-stream: 2000 draws of the integer port: sum, extremes and the last draw (a drifting state shows late)
sources.simulateCoverage.analytic-control: one tree of n blocks: the naive Wilson coverage is a finite sum over the binomial or beta-binomial distribution (scipy.stats)
sources.varianceComponents.unbalanced: Henderson's method I written here from the documented sums of squares and expected mean squares
sources.varianceComponents.binary: pass flags (true / false) are analysed as 1 / 0
sources.varianceComponents.negative-estimate: a negative moment estimate is reported as solved and truncated at 0 for the variance and the shares
sources.varianceComponents.not-estimable: a level with one child per parent has no degrees of freedom: estimate 0, not estimable
sources.varianceComponents.mean-and-n: n and the grand mean of the values
sources.wilsonEffective.all-pass: every block passed: each cluster counts once (n_eff = clusters)
sources.wilsonEffective.all-fail: no block passed: each cluster counts once
sources.wilsonEffective.single-cluster: one cluster: n_eff = n and the normal quantile (no degrees of freedom)
sources.wilsonEffective.no-spread: clusters with identical rates have no spread: n_eff = n
sources.wilsonEffective.capped-at-n: clusters more balanced than a binomial draw would give (a negative intraclass correlation): n_eff would exceed n and is capped at n
sources.wilsonEffective.t-widens: the Student t quantile gives a wider interval than the normal one for the same clusters
sources.hierarchicalBetaBinomial.large-trees: trees of more than 64 blocks take the log-gamma path: a fine numerical integration agrees
sources.hierarchicalBetaBinomial.all-pass: every block passed: the interval still has width and holds the rate
sources.hierarchicalBetaBinomial.two-trees: very few trees give a very wide interval
sources.hierarchicalBetaBinomial.single-block-tr: trees of one block (the repeats of a golden run once): the mean of the flags and a wide interval
sources.hierarchicalBetaBinomial.order-and-dupli: the same trees in another order, or a tree repeated as separate entries, give one interval
sources.sibling.chiSquareSf-infinite: scipy.stats.chi2.sf at Infinity for several degrees of freedom
sources.sibling.mean-no-overflow: the mean of equal finite values is that value, and values that cancel give 0 (exact rational arithmetic)
sources.sibling.hillNumber-near-one: the Hill number is continuous in q: near q = 1 it is exp(Shannon entropy) (to 1e-5 relative for |q - 1| up to 1e-6)
sources.valid-odd.kolmogorovSf: the Kolmogorov survival function at and beyond the ends
sources.valid-odd.benjaminiHochberg: no hypotheses: empty lists and no threshold (scipy.stats.false_discovery_control([]) is empty)
sources.valid-odd.betaQuantile: the quantile at p = 0 and p = 1 is the end of the support
sources.valid-odd.binomialCdf: scipy.stats.binom.cdf below 0 and at or above n
sources.valid-odd.mde: a baseline of 0 has no detectable drop (effect null); a baseline of 1 does
sources.valid-odd.hillNumber: negative orders are defined: (sum 1 / p)^(1 / 2) at q = -1
sources.valid-odd.wilson: k = 0 and k = n are valid and give the closed form (exact decimals)
